The demonstration was released on November 4, 2026. Mistral presented it as an end-to-end run, covering everything from first discovery to a finished fix. [...] The model goes by Mistral Large 4, though it also carries the nickname “Le Chonk.”

results.content:

“Subsequent safeguard updates are applied to our managed API and future model releases, rather than automatically updating downloaded checkpoints,” Stock said. results.title: Mistral’s New ‘Le Chonk’ AI Model Is Big, Open and Now Available for Download - CNET
results.content:
On the heels of the recent rollouts of Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, Mistral Large 4. The model – affectionately known as “Le Chonk” – was available in public preview earlier this month. Now, after weeks of additional reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and assessing it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials, the Mistral team announced Thursday that ML4 is available for download. [...] “The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations,” Mistral said in its announcement. “We’ve put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity.”

More from CNET [...] Earlier this month, I spoke with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – what they’re calling the best open model built in the West – and its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.

## Key capabilities of Mistral Large 4

results.title: Mistral releases latest AI model for download, giving companies more control over their cybersecurity | Euronews
results.content:
The release follows a preview of ML4 on 6 October. Since then, Mistral has spent the last three weeks reinforcing the model's learning, testing it with customers and partners under real-world conditions.

“ML4 OSS showcases our science team's ability to innovate at speed. Building on the ML4 Preview, the open weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation," said Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral. [...] Mistral says ML4 can turn 2D blueprints into usable 3D models using computer-aided design (CAD) software, analyse large volumes of data to support financial decision-making and use satellite and aerial imagery to detect wildfires, track crop health and monitor risks to power lines.

The French firm says the release of ML4 is part of a new generation of models spanning all modalities and that they plan to release more models from this generation in the coming months. [...] Mistral has released the weights for its latest large flagship AI model, Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed “Le Chonk”, claiming improvements in coding and cyber defence as Europe seeks to build alternatives to US and Chinese technology.

results.title: Mistral AI makes the trained model parameters of Mistral Large 4 available – MSP Business
results.content: Mistral AI has made its latest AI model, Mistral Large 4, nicknamed ‘Le Chonk’, available for use on organisations’ own infrastructure. The multimodal model has 1 trillion parameters and, according to the French company, was trained entirely in European data centres. Mistral claims the model ranks among the best-performing open AI models for software development and defensive cybersecurity. Organisations can download the model, run it independently and adapt it to their own applications. [...] The model was released as a public preview earlier this month. Since then, Mistral AI has trained it further using reinforcement learning. According to the company, the model achieves the highest scores on software development benchmarks, including FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.0. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral AI says Mistral Large 4 achieves scores comparable to those of GLM-5.3, while using an average of 47 per cent fewer tokens per task.

content: On the heels of the recent rollouts of Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, Mistral Large 4. The model – affectionately known as “Le Chonk” – was available in public preview earlier this month. Now, after weeks of additional reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and assessing it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials, the Mistral team announced Thursday that ML4 is available for download. [...] “The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations,” Mistral said in its announcement. “We’ve put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity.”

More from CNET [...] Earlier this month, I spoke with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – what they’re calling the best open model built in the West – and its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.

content: The release follows a preview of ML4 on 6 October. Since then, Mistral has spent the last three weeks reinforcing the model's learning, testing it with customers and partners under real-world conditions.

“ML4 OSS showcases our science team's ability to innovate at speed. Building on the ML4 Preview, the open weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation," said Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral. [...] Mistral says ML4 can turn 2D blueprints into usable 3D models using computer-aided design (CAD) software, analyse large volumes of data to support financial decision-making and use satellite and aerial imagery to detect wildfires, track crop health and monitor risks to power lines.

The French firm says the release of ML4 is part of a new generation of models spanning all modalities and that they plan to release more models from this generation in the coming months. [...] Mistral has released the weights for its latest large flagship AI model, Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed “Le Chonk”, claiming improvements in coding and cyber defence as Europe seeks to build alternatives to US and Chinese technology.

[13] title: Mistral AI makes the trained model parameters of Mistral Large 4 available – MSP Business
url: https://mspbusiness.com/en/technology-and-architecture/mistral-ai-makes-the-trained-model-parameters-of-mistral-large-4-available
published: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 13:00:00 GMT
content: Mistral AI has made its latest AI model, Mistral Large 4, nicknamed ‘Le Chonk’, available for use on organisations’ own infrastructure. The multimodal model has 1 trillion parameters and, according to the French company, was trained entirely in European data centres. Mistral claims the model ranks among the best-performing open AI models for software development and defensive cybersecurity. Organisations can download the model, run it independently and adapt it to their own applications. [...] The model was released as a public preview earlier this month. Since then, Mistral AI has trained it further using reinforcement learning. According to the company, the model achieves the highest scores on software development benchmarks, including FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.0. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral AI says Mistral Large 4 achieves scores comparable to those of GLM-5.3, while using an average of 47 per cent fewer tokens per task.

message.content:
## Recent developments
* **Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") Open Weights Release:** Mistral AI officially released the open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter flagship model, Mistral Large 4, following an initial preview period [3, 9, 13]. The model was trained entirely in European data centers [13].
* **Cybersecurity & Agentic Coding Focus:** Mistral emphasized the model's capabilities in defensive cybersecurity and software development [13]. Demonstrations showcased the model deploying 133 multi-agents to successfully find, verify, and patch a real-world Django vulnerability [6]. 
* **Strategic Partnerships:** Orange Cyberdefense joined Mistral's design partner program to integrate Mistral Large 4 into penetration testing and incident response services [7]. Additionally, SAP expanded its enterprise integration, hosting Mistral models locally with a fully sovereign SAP Sovereign Cloud version planned for early 2027 [4].
* **Safety vs. Open-Source Debate:** Mistral acknowledged that while the model has built-in safeguards, its open-weight availability carries a potential uplift for conducting real cyberattacks, noting that subsequent safeguard updates will apply to managed APIs rather than downloaded checkpoints [9].

## Talking points
* **Model Performance and Efficiency:** How post-preview reinforcement learning drove Mistral Large 4's accuracy on Terminal-Bench 4.0 up to 41%, matching competitors like GLM-5.3 while using fewer tokens per task [5, 13].
* **Multi-Agent Orchestration:** The implications of using massive agent swarms (such as the 133-agent Django vulnerability patch demonstration) for automated software maintenance and security operations [6].
* **Sovereignty and Enterprise Adoption:** Leveraging local deployments on infrastructure like SAP and design partnerships with firms like Orange Cyberdefense to meet strict European regulatory and data residency mandates [4, 7, 13].
* **Security Guardrails in Open Models:** Managing the dual-use risk of releasing powerful cyber-capable open-weight models when post-release safety updates cannot be retroactively pushed to downloaded checkpoints [9].

## Open questions
* How will Mistral address the security community's concerns regarding the unpatchable nature of open-weight checkpoints if malicious actors exploit the model's cyberattack uplift potential [9]?
* What are the specific hardware and infrastructure requirements for enterprises wanting to independently run and fine-tune a 1-trillion-parameter model locally [13]?
* Following the recent index shifts, how does Mistral plan to address competitive positioning against rapidly evolving closed and open models on global evaluation benchmarks [1]?
